title: SystemFont.is_script_supported incorrectly reports if font supports Latin script
body:
### Tested versions

v4.3.stable.official [77dcf97d8]

### System information

Godot v4.3.stable - macOS 15.3.0 - Vulkan (Mobile) - integrated Apple M2 Pro - Apple M2 Pro (10 Threads)

### Issue description

Font.is_script_supported() can be used to determine if a font is able to render characters from a specific script (such as Latin, Arabic, Thai etc). SystemFont inherits this and it can be used to determine if the matching system installed font supports a specified script. I'm trying to use this in a font selector control to filter out and show only fonts supporting a specific script. 

However, I've noticed when testing for Latin script support using `is_script_supported("Latn")` this seems to return incorrect results for many fonts, mostly TrueType format fonts, but also some PostScript and possibly also OpenType fonts.

For example the two macOS system arabic only TrueType fonts Beirut and Bahgdad (see details on these from macOS system font manager below) both return true on `is_script_supported("Latn")`, when they do not support Latin script. And since these should be available on all macOS systems preinstalled it should be a good test case. 

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c2628395-4c34-4958-b9e0-4baa8b82c4c2)

### Steps to reproduce

To reproduce on macOS you can use the code below. To test on other systems you can just change the font name to other installed fonts without support for Latin script.

```
var font:SystemFont = SystemFont.new()
var font_family_name:String = "Beirut" #This is a system default arabic only font on macOS 15
font.font_names = [font_family_name]
print("Font '"+font_family_name+"' supports Latin script: "+str(font.is_script_supported("Latn"))) #prints true should be false
```

I've also found multiple instances of false negatives, where fonts that the font manager report as supporting Latin would return false on font.is_script_supported("Latn"). This includes the macOS system standard font "Thonburi" (with support for Cyrillic, Latin and Thai) that reports false 

```
var font:SystemFont = SystemFont.new()
var font_family_name:String = "Thonburi" #This is a system default Cyrillic, Latin and Thai font on macOS 15
font.font_names = [font_family_name]
print("Font '"+font_family_name+"' supports Latin script: "+str(font.is_script_supported("Latn"))) #prints false should be true
```

As SystemFont has a fallback "best match" style fallback one theory I is that it could be in some cases that this is just indicating that it's failing to load the intended font family, and following that it is reporting the is_script_supported("Latn") result from whatever fallback font it has selected in these cases, and this fallback might support other scripts. This could explain the arabic font cases, as the default system font fallback would certainly support Latin. But it would not explain the false negative cases. 

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Code above should be sufficient, at least on macOS as the system fonts should be available to anyone.
